claim_en: ויכלא ("and it was RESTRAINED") — the Masorah pair, both in the Torah: the rain restrained (8:2) and the people RESTRAINED FROM BRINGING (Exod 36:6 — the Tabernacle donors told to stop): "by Israel's merit the rain ceased" (Kitzur). SNAPSHOT: exactly two tokens.
הגשם ("the rain") — the gimel carries a dagesh (doubling dot). SNAPSHOT agrees.

ותנח ("and it RESTED") — the Kitzur's rest-pair: the ark rests on Ararat (8:4) and "the spirit RESTED upon them" (Num 11:26, Eldad and Medad): "the holy spirit rested on those left in the ark." SNAPSHOT holds three consonant-twins — the pair, plus Potiphar's wife LAYING the garment (39:16), a different stem the Masorah's rest-pair rightly excludes.

אררט ("Ararat") — the Kitzur's trio spans to Sennacherib's assassins who "escaped to the land of Ararat" (II Kings 19:37 / Isaiah 37:38), with the tradition's board-homily (the killer took a plank of the ark: "this is the god who saved Noah"). Torah-side: the mountain-name's only token — an inheritance edge to the Prophets.

ושוב ("and returning") — the Kitzur's trio: the waters going-and-returning (8:3), the raven going-out-and-returning (8:7), and Ezekiel's living creatures RUNNING-and-returning (Ezek 1:14, with the fire-river homily). Torah-side: exactly the two flood tokens (Jacob's return-command, 31:13, is another form and stands apart) — the third leg is an inheritance edge to Ezekiel.
יבשת ("the drying of the waters") — the bet with CHOLAM (the o-vowel). SNAPSHOT agrees.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:11 (Radak, Mikhlol and Roots — against Rashi)
claim_en: טרף בפיה ("a torn-off [leaf] in her mouth") — Radak: ALL QAMATZ (the long a-vowel twice), "for it is an adjective describing the leaf — torn — NOT as Rashi's reading of the verse" (who takes it as a verb): a recorded grammatical dispute. SNAPSHOT points it qamatz-qamatz — the Radak camp.

טרף — the Kitzur's pair leaps to Hosea: "for He has TORN, and He will heal us" (Hos 6:1) — "as there a breaking, so here: she broke it from the tree, and by this he knew the waters had lightened." Torah-side: this pointed form's only token (the tearing-infinitives of Joseph's coat are other forms) — an inheritance edge to Hosea.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:13 (the two camps)
claim_en: ויהי באחת ("and it was in the six hundred and first year") — the books split into camps: some read telisha [gedola] ("detached," the DISJUNCTIVE sign) on ויהי with the bet of באחת DAGESH; others the small conjunctive sign with bet soft. SNAPSHOT: telisha gedola — the first camp's accent.

באחת — and the same camp's bet DAGESH (doubling dot), the pairing Minchat Shai reports as a package (disjunctive accent → hard bet). SNAPSHOT: bet with dagesh — the package complete, both halves locked.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 8:8 (Or Torah; manuscripts)
claim_en: הקלו ("had the waters LIGHTENED") — first-syllable stress with galgal ("wheel," the day-old-moon accent) on the qof per the manuscripts and Or Torah; SNAPSHOT's chain reads munach — the galgal variant class, recurrence #3 (gen_11's G11-16, gen_14's G14-12).

check.note: galgal absent from SNAPSHOT mark inventory at this token (munach); manuscript accent-variant class, banked with G11-16/G14-12

claim_en: THE WATERS ARE PROVEN TO HAVE BEEN HOT, FROM THE VERB OF THEIR COOLING. Our 8:1 says the waters וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ (va-yashoku, 'abated'), and the same verb describes a king's wrath being ASSUAGED - which means cooled. By verbal analogy Rav Chisda concludes the flood waters were scalding: 'they sinned with boiling passion and were punished with boiling water'. A physical property of this unit's world-state is derived from a shared verb, not from any description.

check.note: A physical state inferred by verbal analogy (middah E7) from the verb used to end it.

source: Rosh Hashanah 10b:6; Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 1:1:3; Tosefta Rosh Hashanah (Lieberman) 1:3
claim_en: LIVE CALENDAR LAW STANDS ON OUR 8:13's DATE FORMULA. R. Meir derives the rule that ONE DAY IN A YEAR COUNTS AS A YEAR from this verse's ink: one day into the six hundred and first year, and the verse already calls it a year. The same verse is used as the calendar system's stress test - the objection that the count works only if the flood year is not counted is resolved only on the Tishrei reckoning - and the Tosefta's rule that months are counted from Nisan is set against our verse's ordinals.

check.note: A general rule of legal reckoning derived from this unit's own date operator, and the same operator used to stress-test the calendar system.

claim_en: THE DOVE'S OLIVE-LEAF VERB IS PARSED TWO OPPOSITE WAYS AND BOTH ARE CARRIED. טָרָף (taraf) at our 8:11 is read as KILLED - the leaf torn off, in the vocabulary later used of Joseph - and as SUSTENANCE, in the dove's own prayer: 'may my sustenance be bitter as the olive and dependent on YOUR hands rather than sweet as honey and dependent on flesh and blood'. The dove is also read typologically: had it found rest it would not have returned, which becomes the figure of exile.

check.note: One verb read as killing and as sustenance at two seats, both carried without merger.

claim_en: THE RAVEN ARGUES BACK, AND IS KEPT FOR A LATER UNIT. The sending of the raven at our 8:7 is read as a recorded exchange: the raven objects that it is of a species taken only in twos, that it is being spared over the species taken in sevens, and asks whether it is its mate that is wanted. It is judged unfit for food or for offering - and the reason given for keeping it alive at all is that Elijah will later need ravens to feed him. A creature preserved in this unit because a much later unit requires it.

check.note: A dispatch operator whose subject is recorded arguing with the sender, preserved for a use in a far later book.

claim_en: THE REMEMBERING OF OUR 8:1 IS READ AS COVERING THE WHOLE ARK'S MANIFEST, and the flood's two halves are typed by which geography they used: judgment came through the DEPTHS, broken open at 7:11, and kindness through the MOUNTAINS, on which the ark came to rest. The unit's own topography is read as the instrument of two different divine attributes.

check.note: The unit's geography typed as the instrument of two attributes, and the remembering operator scoped to the whole manifest.
